result.notes:
Per-criterion: C1 MET (live read by me: published_at TIMESTAMP REQUIRED + ingested_at TIMESTAMP REQUIRED, distinct, fetched_at gone; P3 mutant proves the live oracle drives the verdict). C2 MET (provenance STRING REQUIRED in BOTH tables live; 3 independent mutants killed on the live-vs-backfill discrimination). C3 MET (all three asserts in one test; c3_no_record, c3_log_debug and c3_raise each killed it separately). C4 MET (`after == before + 1` strict increase; c3_wrong_key killed it, so the counter is keyed on the right table -- not merely attribute existence). C5 MET (two-adapter registry flow + a scan proven live by the known-member recall test). C6 MET (git diff over exactly the two paths empty; key check reproduces False/False).

NOTE-level, non-blocking: (a) OFFLINE DEGRADATION -- forcing the live BQ read to fail makes C1/C2 pass on the checked-in snapshot (P1: 9 passed), so in a no-network CI the oracle degrades to a constant the author wrote. On this rig the live read succeeds and is load-bearing (P3 fails 2 tests), and I confirmed the live schema independently, so it is not vacuous here; the author partially disclosed this shape in the honest m6-rewrite note. Worth a `pytest.fail` instead of a silent fallback when BQ is unreachable, or an explicit skip marker. (b) The block labelled "Verification (verbatim)" in experiment_results_83.0.md elides the `in 4.96s` suffix and the RequestsDependencyWarning line; the 9 progress dots match "9 passed" so it is not spliced and every number reproduces exactly, but a block labelled verbatim should be regenerated, not trimmed (the live_check DOES disclose its bq-CLI warning elision -- apply the same discipline here). (c) The fetched_at grep claim ("ONLY the 7 protected calendar_events sites plus comments and the compat lookup") reproduces exactly on the 7 calendar sites, but the enumeration omits one hit: backend/tests/test_phase_83_0_news_corpus_persistence.py:97, the new negative assertion. Benign, but the set was described as complete. (d) `_serialize_article` silently coerces an invalid provenance to "live" (bq_writer.py:163-168) -- the coercion default is the more dangerous of the two values; "unknown" or a recorded failure would be safer given there are no BQ CHECK constraints.

Trading-domain heuristics: no kill_switch / stop-loss / perf_metrics / position-sizing path touched; no secret in the diff; bq-schema-migration-safety does NOT fire because no live table was altered or dropped (both were created fresh -- proven by REQUIRED provenance being present); the pre-existing `except Exception` fail-open in _insert_rows is now instrumented, which is a strict improvement over the swallowed-warning baseline it replaces. The refuted "BQ ignores unknown keys" docstring correction (D2) is a genuine and well-cited fix.

Evidence provenance disclosure: all live evidence in this verdict was captured BY ME (BQ reads, pytest runs, ruff runs, mutation injections, greps), not read from Main's artifacts. No UI claims in this step, so section 1c does not apply and no Playwright capture was required. Mutations were run entirely in-process via sys.modules injection -- zero repo writes, nothing to restore; the qa-write-guard hook correctly blocked my one attempt to stage a plugin file in scratchpad.

Path to PASS on cycle 2: queue the --backfill provenance gap as its own pending masterplan step (per the standing rule) or thread `provenance="backfill"` at scripts/smoketest/phase6_e2e.py:112, add the gap to the Scope disclosures, and record the pre-existing ruff F401 state (or clean the two dead imports at backend/news/fetcher.py:39). Then re-spawn a fresh Q/A on the CHANGED evidence -- that is the documented cycle-2 flow, not verdict-shopping.
